result.summary: Introduces a `util::NotNull<SmartPtrType>` template wrapper (along with `NotNullUniquePtr` and `NotNullSharedPtr` aliases) that enforces and documents non-null invariants for smart pointer types. The wrapper checks non-nullness upon construction, deletes null assignments and comparisons, and is applied across several codebase areas including `CDBWrapper`, `CNode`, `CoinsViewOverlay`, and `CTxMemPool::GetChangeSet()`.
result.problem: The C++ standard library lacks a type to specify that a smart pointer cannot be null. Consequently, functions handling non-null smart pointers must repeatedly rely on manual runtime assertions or comments to guarantee non-nullness before dereferencing.
evidence: PR description: 'Fix all issues by adding util::NotNull<SmartPtrType>, which documents (and checks) that the inner pointer is never null. This type can be used when passing never-null smart pointers between functions. It removes the need to Assert() the pointer before dereference.'
Commit fa2e546978: 'This allows to drop the runtime Assert every time the context is accessed, because the type is known to be not null at compile-time.'
Description states that this closes long-standing issue #24423.
result.scope_notes: Adds a new header utility (`src/util/not_null.h`) and unit tests, followed by four commits adopting the wrapper in `CDBWrapper`, `CoinsViewOverlay`, `CNode`, and `CTxMemPool`.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased without fundamental architectural changes to `util::NotNull` or its initial adoption sites.
result.card: Introduces `util::NotNull<SmartPtrType>` to enforce and document non-null smart pointer invariants at initialization time, addressing long-standing issue #24423. It eliminates repetitive runtime defensive assertions prior to dereferencing and clarifies pointer contracts at function boundaries. The PR includes comprehensive unit tests and applies the wrapper to smart pointers in `CDBWrapper`, `CNode`, `CoinsViewOverlay`, and `CTxMemPool`.

risk.why: A flaw in pointer lifetime semantics, movement, or assertion logic could cause unexpected runtime assertion failures or aborts in sensitive network, mempool, or database code.
